summary: The original two-node TP=16 GLM-5.2 deadlock could not be reproduced with one gfx950 GPU and no model weights. Source inspection shows the reported overlap-scheduler command defaults to the CPU process group, so the reporter's standalone NCCL collective does not test the implicated Gloo path. Local 2-rank and 16-rank Gloo contract fixtures completed with heterogeneous active/idle metadata; no corrective source change is justified without per-rank evidence from the original topology.

tests.what_was_measured: Four existing CPU unit tests covering DP1 gather skipping and decode-to-extend voting passed.
Two localhost Gloo ranks completed MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather with heterogeneous extend/idle metadata and agreed on global token counts.
Sixteen localhost Gloo ranks, shaped as dp_size=2 and tp_size=8, completed the checked-out metadata gather and agreed on [64, 0] token counts.
The retained evidence fixture compiles and the patch has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: raw/gpu_inventory.txt and raw/torch_gpu_probe.txt show the assigned single gfx950 GPU and a basic ROCm tensor probe, but no issue-specific SGLang GPU serving path was executed because the report requires two H100 nodes, 16 ranks, and unavailable GLM-5.2 W4AFP8 weights.

remaining_limitations: No second node or 16 assigned GPUs were available.
The reported H100/CUDA/NCCL hardware and GLM-5.2 W4AFP8 weights were unavailable.
Localhost Gloo completion cannot exclude cross-node Gloo transport failure or scheduler collective-order divergence.
No model architecture, speculative decoding, semantic accuracy, or distributed serving behavior was validated.
